# Explain a Project Architecture Through a Technical Deep Dive

[← Atlassian](../README.md) · [Every Atlassian question](../../atlassian.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/explain-a-project-architecture-through-a-technical-deep-dive)

---

Get ready to deliver a thorough technical walkthrough of a system you helped build. Use an architecture diagram to explain its parts, then stand behind the key design decisions, the interfaces, and the failure behavior of each component you owned.

### Limits and Assumptions

- Ground your talk in a real project, and make it clear where your responsibilities end and the rest of the system begins.
- Lead with a clean diagram and one end-to-end request or data flow before going deeper into the specifics.
- Go deep enough technically to cover storage, processing, dependencies, and failure recovery wherever they matter for your system.
- Never fabricate scale or performance numbers; instead point to actual measurements you possess and call out assumptions you'd need to validate.

### Clarifying Questions to Raise

- Does the interviewer want to follow a request, a background job, or a failure scenario first?
- Which component do they want to zoom into beyond the high-level diagram?
- Should the conversation center on a past design decision or on a limitation you intend to tackle next?

> **Hint:** Make every edge in your diagram easy to talk through For any important connection, be ready to name the data, protocol or interface, who owns it, how retries are handled, and what happens when it fails.

### What a Solid Response Includes

- A diagram that breaks out components and state stores and makes ownership explicit.
- An end-to-end flow described with actual interface and data contracts.
- For each component discussed deeply, a design choice and the alternative you considered.
- How failures are spotted, how recovery happens, and proof that it works.
- A crisp line separating what is already built from what you'd improve next.

### Follow-up Questions That Might Come Up

- Which dependency failure would hit users the hardest, and how would the system react?
- If the load or product requirements outgrew the original design scope, what would you change first?

To sum up: prepare an architecture deep dive with an end-to-end diagram, clear component ownership, interface contracts, design alternatives, and evidence of failure recovery.

This question was taken from the complete Atlassian Software Engineer interview experience.
